intended_object: An auxiliary operator for a fixed-point (Picard/contraction) argument in the library's Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg / Leray development. It is the Duhamel map linearized around a fixed L² trajectory g: v ↦ e^{tΔ}b − ∫₀ᵗ (Stokes kernel at time τ)(regularised tensor of g, v)(t−τ) dτ, acting on continuous paths in the Bessel space H^{2k} on [0,T]. The description comes from the docstring and the body.
explanation:
This is a project-specific device for a proof, not a standard mathematical object with a textbook definition. It packages the linearized mild-solution map of the mollified Navier–Stokes/Leray system as a continuous path into H^{2k}. That path is meant to be fed to a contraction-mapping argument. Several arguments are proof bookkeeping: the bound B, the proofs hB and hg, and the constant C are used only to prove continuity of the Duhamel integral.

The construction itself looks consistent. The integrand `regularisedBesselShiftedStokesIntegrand` vanishes unless 0 < τ < t, so ∫₀ᵀ is effectively ∫₀ᵗ, which is the usual Duhamel term. The heat term is the heat semigroup applied to b at time t. The tensor path clamps time to [0,T], which is just how the path is extended outside the interval.

Mathlib has no general counterpart of this specific linearized mild map. Since it is an internal construction for the library's existence proof, the right category is not_a_mathematical_object.
